review.market_summary: 1) Fed may have to hike: the hot October CPI has rates traders pricing a December hike and possibly a series of hikes (WSJ: 'bigger and faster rate rises'). The dollar is at a 19-month high and gold has fallen to $3,973, but stocks have barely adjusted (SPY -0.9%, QQQ -0.2% over 5 days). 2) Chip export controls are tightening during an Nvidia governance crisis: the Jensen Huang alleged-spy scandal has revived China chip-curb pressure ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, and the US is widening AI chip controls to seven nations. NVDA is down 13% in 5 days, but money has rotated into AMD and chip-equipment names (+6-13%) instead of leaving the sector. 3) Oil news points both ways: OPEC+ output rose about 2M bpd and Brent is below $90, while Israel is preparing a possible strike on Iran. No clean trade there.
